claim: Design of complex alpha-beta protein topologies poses a challenge because of the large number of alternative packing arrangements.
source: Design of complex alpha-beta protein topologies poses a challenge because of the large number of alternative packing arrangements.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the field of protein design.

claim: A similar challenge presumably limited the emergence of large and complex protein topologies in evolution.
source: A similar challenge presumably limited the emergence of large and complex protein topologies in evolution.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about evolutionary constraints, indicated by the word 'presumably'.

claim: Protein topologies with six and seven-stranded beta sheets can be designed by insertion of one de novo designed beta sheet containing protein into another such that the two beta sheets are merged to form a single extended sheet, followed by amino acid sequence optimization at the newly formed strand-strand, strand-helix, and helix-helix interfaces.
source: Here, we demonstrate that protein topologies with six and seven-stranded beta sheets can be designed by insertion of one de novo designed beta sheet containing protein into another such that the two beta sheets are merged to form a single extended sheet, followed by amino acid sequence optimization at the newly formed strand-strand, strand-helix, and helix-helix interfaces.
evidence: This is the primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Crystal structures of two such designs closely match the computational design models.
source: Crystal structures of two such designs closely match the computational design models.
evidence: This is supported by experimental crystallographic data presented in the Results section.

claim: Searches for similar structures in the SCOP protein domain database yield only weak matches with different beta sheet connectivities.
source: Searches for similar structures in the SCOP protein domain database yield only weak matches with different beta sheet connectivities.
evidence: This is supported by computational analysis of structural databases described in the Results section.

claim: A similar beta sheet fusion mechanism may have contributed to the emergence of complex beta sheets during natural protein evolution.
source: A similar beta sheet fusion mechanism may have contributed to the emergence of complex beta sheets during natural protein evolution.
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis about evolutionary mechanisms, indicated by the word 'may'.

claim: Multi-domain proteins likely evolved through simple linear concatenation of successive domains onto the polypeptide chain or through the insertion of one or more continuous sequences into the middle of another, now discontinuous domain.
source: Multi-domain proteins likely evolved through simple linear concatenation of successive domains onto the polypeptide chain or through the insertion of one or more continuous sequences into the middle of another, now discontinuous domain (Aroul-Selvam et al., 2004; Berrondo et al., 2008; Lupas et al., 2001; Pandya et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature on protein evolution.

claim: New proteins have been engineered from existing domains by simple linear concatenation or insertion of one domain into another.
source: By analogy, new proteins have been engineered from existing domains by simple linear concatenation or insertion of one domain into another (Ay et al., 1998; Collinet et al., 2000; Cutler et al., 2009; Doi and Yanagawa, 1999; Edwards et al., 2008; Guntas and Ostermeier, 2004; Ostermeier, 2005).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous protein engineering work.

claim: How individual domains evolved is much less clear.
source: How individual domains evolved, in contrast, is much less clear.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about gaps in understanding of protein evolution.

claim: There is no evidence that complex beta sheet topologies can be formed by insertion of one fold into another.
source: but to our knowledge, there is no evidence that complex beta sheet topologies can be formed in this manner.
evidence: This is stated as a gap in current knowledge based on the authors' review of the literature.

claim: Assembly of large and complex beta sheets poses a challenge for de novo protein design.
source: assembly of large and complex beta sheets poses a challenge for de novo protein design.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the field of protein design.

claim: A first extended sheet protein was created by inserting a designed ferredoxin domain into a beta turn of the designed TOP7 protein to create a half-barrel structure, with the two sheets fused into a single seven strand sheet flanked by four helices.
source: A first extended sheet protein was created by inserting a designed ferredoxin domain into a beta turn of the designed TOP7 protein to create a half-barrel structure, with the two sheets fused into a single seven strand sheet flanked by four helices (Figure 1A).
evidence: This describes the experimental design and is supported by the figure showing the structure.

claim: The CD spectra of the ferredoxin-TOP7 fusion show both alpha and beta structures.
source: The CD spectra show both alpha and beta structures (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental CD spectroscopy data shown in the figure.

claim: Two crystal structures of the ferredoxin-TOP7 fusion (NESG target OR327) were solved by molecular replacement and refined to 2.49 Å (PDB entry 4KYZ) and 2.96 Å (PDB entry 4KY3) resolutions.
source: Two crystal structures (NESG target OR327) were solved by molecular replacement and refined to 2.49 Å (PDB entry 4KYZ) and 2.96 Å (PDB entry 4KY3) resolutions.
evidence: This is supported by experimental crystallographic data.

claim: The ferredoxin-TOP7 structure shows excellent agreement with the design model, particularly in low B-factor regions, with C-alpha RMSD ranging from 1.76 to 1.85 Å among the four protomers in the crystal.
source: The structure shows excellent agreement with the design model (Figure 2A), particularly in low B-factor regions, with C-alpha RMSD ranging from 1.76 to 1.85 Å among the four protomers in the crystal.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative comparison of crystal structure to design model.

claim: The relative orientation of the strands packed against the helices in the ferredoxin-TOP7 fusion is close to that in the design model.
source: The relative orientation of the strands packed against the helices is close to that in the design model, and core sidechains at the designed interfaces are in very similar conformations in the design model and crystal (Figure 2B,C).
evidence: This is supported by structural comparison shown in the figures.

claim: Core sidechains at the designed interfaces in the ferredoxin-TOP7 fusion are in very similar conformations in the design model and crystal.
source: The relative orientation of the strands packed against the helices is close to that in the design model, and core sidechains at the designed interfaces are in very similar conformations in the design model and crystal (Figure 2B,C).
evidence: This is supported by structural comparison shown in the figures.

claim: A second extended sheet protein was created by inserting one designed ferredoxin domain into another to create a half-barrel structure with four alpha helices and six beta strands.
source: A second extended sheet protein was created by inserting one designed ferredoxin domain into another to create a half-barrel structure with four alpha helices and six beta strands (Figure 1B).
evidence: This describes the experimental design and is supported by the figure showing the structure.

claim: A beta turn segment between two beta strands of the host ferredoxin was removed and the resulting cut-points in the host beta strands were linked to two beta strand cut-points in the insert, fusing the two strand pairs into a single, longer pair at the center of a six-stranded beta sheet.
source: A beta turn segment between two beta strands of the host ferredoxin was removed and the resulting cut-points in the host beta strands were linked to two beta strand cut-points in the insert, fusing the two strand pairs into a single, longer pair at the center of a six-stranded beta sheet.
evidence: This describes the design methodology used to create the fusion protein.

claim: CD spectra show that the ferredoxin-ferredoxin fusion protein contains both alpha and beta structures.
source: CD spectra show that the protein contains both alpha and beta structures (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental CD spectroscopy data shown in the figure.

claim: Crystals of the ferredoxin-ferredoxin fusion were obtained which diffracted to 3.3Å resolution.
source: Crystals were obtained which diffracted to 3.3Å resolution.
evidence: This is supported by experimental crystallographic data.

claim: Molecular replacement using the computational design models yielded a solution for the ferredoxin-ferredoxin fusion (PDB entry 5CW9).
source: Molecular replacement using the computational design models (DiMaio et al., 2013) yielded a solution for which the refinement statistics are shown in Supplementary file 1 (PDB entry 5CW9).
evidence: This is supported by experimental crystallographic data and methods citation.

claim: Attempts to improve the refinement statistics of the ferredoxin-ferredoxin fusion by rebuilding portions of the model proved unsuccessful, possibly due to a register shift or dynamic fluctuations in the structure.
source: Attempts to improve these statistics by rebuilding portions of the model proved unsuccessful, possibly due to a register shift or dynamic fluctuations in the structure (perhaps corresponding to slightly 'molten-globule'-like behavior) that are difficult to computationally model.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the crystallographic refinement challenges.

claim: Unbiased low-resolution omit maps suggest that the overall topology of the ferredoxin-ferredoxin fusion is correct.
source: However, unbiased low-resolution omit maps suggest that the overall topology is correct (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by crystallographic electron density maps shown in the figure.

claim: In the ferredoxin-ferredoxin fusion model that displays the best refinement statistics, the protein backbone was similar to the design model with a C-alpha RMSD value of 2 Å.
source: In the model that displays the best refinement statistics, the protein backbone was similar to the design model with a C-alpha RMSD value of 2 Å (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative comparison of crystal structure to design model.

claim: The fused beta sheet in the ferredoxin-ferredoxin fusion aligns with the design model, while the inter-domain helices shift slightly to accommodate the inter-domain interface.
source: The fused beta sheet aligns with the design model, while the inter-domain helices shift slightly to accommodate the inter-domain interface.
evidence: This is supported by structural comparison of crystal structure to design model.

claim: The sidechain packing between the newly juxtaposed beta strands in the ferredoxin-ferredoxin fusion succeeded in anchoring the secondary structure elements in their intended orientations.
source: The sidechain packing between the newly juxtaposed beta strands succeeded in anchoring the secondary structure elements in their intended orientations, but the low resolution of the crystal structure prevents evaluation of the atomic-level accuracy of the design (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis of the crystal structure.

claim: The low resolution of the ferredoxin-ferredoxin fusion crystal structure prevents evaluation of the atomic-level accuracy of the design.
source: The sidechain packing between the newly juxtaposed beta strands succeeded in anchoring the secondary structure elements in their intended orientations, but the low resolution of the crystal structure prevents evaluation of the atomic-level accuracy of the design (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a limitation acknowledged based on the crystallographic data quality.

claim: The TMalign structure-structure comparison method was used to search a 70% sequence non-redundant set of SCOP domains for structure alignments containing a minimum 75% overlap with the designed proteins.
source: To compare the folds of these designed proteins to those in the SCOP v.1.75 domain database (Murzin et al., 1995), the TMalign structure-structure comparison method was used to search a 70% sequence non-redundant set of SCOP domains (Ben-Tal and Kolodny, 2014) for structure alignments containing a minimum 75% overlap with the designed proteins.
evidence: This describes the computational method used for structural comparison, with citations to the database and methods.

claim: The most similar SCOP domains to the designed proteins had weak TM-align scores (0.54 and 0.51).
source: The most similar SCOP domains had weak TM-align scores (0.54 and 0.51), and the sheets in these matched structures have different connectivities than those of the designs, suggesting that the two designed proteins have novel folds (Figure 4).
evidence: This is supported by computational structural comparison data.

claim: The sheets in the most similar SCOP domains have different connectivities than those of the designed proteins.
source: The most similar SCOP domains had weak TM-align scores (0.54 and 0.51), and the sheets in these matched structures have different connectivities than those of the designs, suggesting that the two designed proteins have novel folds (Figure 4).
evidence: This is supported by computational structural comparison data shown in the figure.

claim: The two designed proteins have novel folds.
source: The most similar SCOP domains had weak TM-align scores (0.54 and 0.51), and the sheets in these matched structures have different connectivities than those of the designs, suggesting that the two designed proteins have novel folds (Figure 4).
evidence: This is inferred from the weak structural similarity scores and different connectivities compared to known structures.

claim: Both designed proteins are similar to a number of SCOP domains over the ferrodoxin-like substructure(s).
source: While there are no domains with globally similar folds, both designed proteins are similar to a number of SCOP domains over the ferrodoxin-like substructure(s) (maps of the proteins to the domain network of Nepomnyachiy et al. (Ben-Tal and Kolodny, 2014) are shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by computational structural comparison data shown in the figure supplement.

claim: The mutations introduced at the redesign stage of the domain insertion design protocol are compatible with the parent fold structures with minimal perturbation of the protein backbone.
source: The mutations introduced at the redesign stage of the domain insertion design protocol are compatible with the parent fold structures with minimal perturbation of the protein backbone (Figure 4—figure supplement 2) suggesting the designed folds would have the potential to evolve from insertion followed by neutral mutational drift of the parent structures.
evidence: This is supported by computational modeling data shown in the figure supplement.

claim: The designed folds would have the potential to evolve from insertion followed by neutral mutational drift of the parent structures.
source: The mutations introduced at the redesign stage of the domain insertion design protocol are compatible with the parent fold structures with minimal perturbation of the protein backbone (Figure 4—figure supplement 2) suggesting the designed folds would have the potential to evolve from insertion followed by neutral mutational drift of the parent structures.
evidence: This is inferred from the computational modeling showing minimal perturbation of parent structures.

claim: Single designed protein domains can be combined into larger domains with complex beta sheet topologies.
source: We have shown that single designed protein domains can be combined into larger domains with complex beta sheet topologies.
evidence: This is the main conclusion supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: This mechanism provides a straightforward route to designing large and complex beta sheet structures capable of scaffolding the pockets and cavities essential for future design of protein functions.
source: This mechanism provides a straightforward route to designing large and complex beta sheet structures capable of scaffolding the pockets and cavities essential for future design of protein functions.
evidence: This is an inference about the potential applications of the demonstrated design approach.

claim: The success in designing larger beta sheet domains by recombining smaller independently folded beta sheet proteins suggests a similar mechanism could have played a role in the evolution of naturally occurring complex beta sheet proteins.
source: Our success in designing larger beta sheet domains by recombining smaller independently folded beta sheet proteins suggests a similar mechanism could have played a role in the evolution of naturally occurring complex beta sheet proteins.
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis about evolutionary mechanisms based on the design results.

claim: Three previously characterized de novo designed protein domains (ferredoxin, rossman 2x2, and top7) were selected to serve as building blocks for recombination through domain insertion.
source: Our design strategy began with selection of three previously characterized de novo designed protein domains to serve as building blocks for recombination through domain insertion: ferredoxin, rossman 2x2, and top7 (Koga et al., 2012).
evidence: This describes the experimental design approach with citation to the source of the building blocks.

claim: Ferredoxin, rossman 2x2, and top7 were chosen because they were the only Rosetta de novo designed protein domains with both alpha and beta secondary structures for which high-resolution experimental structures had been obtained at the time of this work.
source: These three domains were chosen because they were the only Rosetta de novo designed protein domains with both alpha and beta secondary structures for which high-resolution experimental structures had been obtained at the time of this work.
evidence: This explains the rationale for the selection of building blocks based on available structural data.

claim: Insertion points were accepted for residue pair alignment distances of 1 angstrom RMSD or less, replacing host domain segments of less than 5 residues.
source: Insertion points were accepted for residue pair alignment distances of 1 angstrom RMSD or less, replacing host domain segments of less than 5 residues.
evidence: This describes the computational design criteria used in the methodology.

claim: Host and insert were connected by addition of 1–3 residues at the domain junctions using Rosetta Remodel, and 12 models in which this junction formed a continuous beta strand were identified.
source: Host and insert were connected by addition of 1–3 residues at the domain junctions using Rosetta Remodel (Huang et al., 2011), and 12 models in which this junction formed a continuous beta strand were identified.
evidence: This describes the computational design methodology with citation to the software used.

claim: During the design simulation, all amino acid positions within 5 Å of the inter-domain junction interface were redesigned to minimize the predicted free energy of folding with the Rosetta all-atom energy function and a flexible backbone protein design protocol.
source: During the design simulation, all amino acid positions within 5 Å of the inter-domain junction interface were redesigned to minimize the predicted free energy of folding with the Rosetta all-atom energy function and a flexible backbone protein design protocol described previously (Huang et al., 2011).
evidence: This describes the computational design methodology with citation to the protocol.

claim: Final designs were selected based on Rosetta energy, packing metrics, and similarity of the junction backbone geometry to local backbone geometry in the PDB.
source: Final designs were selected based on Rosetta energy, packing metrics, and similarity of the junction backbone geometry to local backbone geometry in the PDB.
evidence: This describes the selection criteria used in the design methodology.

claim: Twelve final domain insertion designs were chosen for expression in Escherichia coli as 6xHis-tag fusions and purified on a Ni-NTA column.
source: Twelve final domain insertion designs were chosen for expression in Escherichia coli as 6xHis-tag fusions and purified on a Ni-NTA column.
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology for protein expression and purification.

claim: Three designs with levels of secondary structure content consistent with the design model were subjected to crystallographic analysis.
source: Purified proteins were evaluated for the presence of alpha/beta secondary structures via circular dichroism spectroscopy (CD), and three with levels of secondary structure content consistent with the design model were subjected to crystallographic analysis.
evidence: This describes the experimental screening and selection process.

claim: One design based on Rossman 2x2 expressed as soluble protein, but no crystal structure could be obtained.
source: One design based on Rossman 2x2 expressed as soluble protein, but no crystal structure could be obtained.
evidence: This reports a negative experimental result.

claim: Crystal structures were obtained for two designed proteins: a ferredoxin-top7 chimera and a ferredoxin-ferredoxin chimera.
source: Crystal structures were obtained for two designed proteins: a ferredoxin-top7 chimera and a ferredoxin-ferredoxin chimera.
evidence: This summarizes the successful experimental outcomes.

claim: The ferredoxin-TOP7 protein (NESF ID OR327) was expressed and purified following standard protocols developed by the NESG for production of selenomethionine-labeled protein samples.
source: The ferredoxin – TOP7 protein (NESF ID OR327) was expressed and purified following standard protocols developed by the NESG for production of selenomethionine-labeled protein samples (Xiao et al., 2010).
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology with citation to the protocols used.

claim: Yields of purified ferredoxin-TOP7 protein were 60-90 mg/L.
source: Yields were 60-–90 mg/L.
evidence: This reports quantitative experimental data on protein expression yields.

claim: The sample purity of ferredoxin-TOP7 was greater than 98%.
source: The sample purity (>98%), molecular weight, and oligomerization state were verified by SDS/PAGE, MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry, and analytic gel filtration followed by static light scattering, respectively.
evidence: This reports quantitative experimental characterization data.

claim: Structures have been deposited in the Protein Data Bank as entries 5CW9, 4KYZ, and 4KY3.
source: Structures have been deposited in the Protein Data Bank as entries 5CW9, 4KYZ, and 4KY3.
evidence: This reports the data deposition information.
